intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Tonight's the night. The time machine in the garage is finally ready.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Every Bible left in 2060 is a digital copy, and nobody can tell anymore which words have been changed.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: So I'm going back to the very beginning, to see it with my own eyes and write it down true.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: My family is home. I should talk to them before I go. The garage is through the living room.

family.name: Mom

talk.speaker: Mom
talk.text: There you are. I made your favorite tonight, just in case it's the last real dinner you get for a while.

talk.speaker: Mom
talk.text: Are you sure you want to do this, sweetheart? The beginning of the world is a long way from our kitchen.

family.question: What do you tell Mom?
options: I'm sure. Someone has to see it with their own eyes.

replies.speaker: Mom
replies.text: You always did want to see things for yourself. Even when you were little, you'd never believe a story until you'd checked it.

replies.speaker: Mom
replies.text: Just promise me you'll be careful. Watch, and write, and don't wander too far.

replies.speaker: Mom
replies.text: Scared is all right. It means you know this matters.

replies.speaker: Mom
replies.text: "Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid... for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest." I'll be praying that over you every day.

after.speaker: Mom
after.text: Now come here and give me a hug before you go. I love you, my {child}.

again.speaker: Mom
again.text: Go on. We'll be right here when you get back. I'll keep your plate warm.

family.name: Dad

talk.speaker: Dad
talk.text: Hey, kiddo. I keep looking at that machine in the garage. It hums even when nobody's touching it.

talk.speaker: Dad
talk.text: Help me understand something. Why go all the way back to the very beginning? Why not start somewhere closer to us?

family.question: What do you tell Dad?
options: If the beginning is wrong, everything after it is too.
I want to see every story in order, as it happened.

replies.speaker: Dad
replies.text: Huh. Like pouring the foundation before you build the walls.

replies.speaker: Dad
replies.text: That makes sense. You can't build a straight house on a crooked foundation.

replies.speaker: Dad
replies.text: One story at a time, in order. That's how your grandma read them to me every night when I was a boy.

replies.speaker: Dad
replies.text: Start with "In the beginning" and keep going. I like that.

after.speaker: Dad
after.text: I'm proud of you. Not just because it's brave, though it is. Because you care about the truth enough to go and find it.

again.speaker: Dad
again.text: Garage door's unlocked. Don't forget your satchel. And your scroll!

family.name: Grandma

talk.speaker: Grandma
talk.text: Come sit by me a minute. My knees aren't going anywhere, but you are.

talk.speaker: Grandma
talk.text: When I was young, I had a Bible made of paper. I could hold it in my hands, and nobody could change a single word without me seeing.

talk.speaker: Grandma
talk.text: Then the books went away, and the screens started saying whatever someone wanted them to say.

talk.speaker: Grandma
talk.text: So tell me, dear. Why does it have to be you?

family.question: What do you tell Grandma?
options: Because I can't stop thinking about it, Grandma.
Because you taught me those words were worth keeping.

replies.speaker: Grandma
replies.text: Maybe that's how you know you're called to it.

replies.speaker: Grandma
replies.text: Young Samuel heard his name in the night and answered, "Speak; for thy servant heareth." Sounds like you're listening too.

replies.speaker: Grandma
replies.text: Oh, sweetheart. Then all my old stories did their job.

replies.speaker: Grandma
replies.text: "The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever." Go and find it standing.

after.speaker: Grandma
after.text: Bring me back a page I can hold, will you? I've saved a spot on my shelf for it.

again.speaker: Grandma
again.text: Go on, now. I'll be right here in my chair, waiting for that page.

family.name: Sam

talk.speaker: Sam
talk.text: Is it true? You're going back to before there were even people?

talk.speaker: Sam
talk.text: Will you see the very first animals? Like, the very first dog ever?

family.question: What do you tell Sam?
options: I'll write down every animal I see, just for you.
I'll bring the whole story back for you to read.

replies.speaker: Sam
replies.text: Every single one? Even the bugs?

replies.speaker: Sam
replies.text: Okay. But if you see Biscuit's great-great-great... a LOT of greats... grandpa, say hi for me.

replies.speaker: Sam
replies.text: A real one? Nobody at my school has ever even seen a real one.

replies.speaker: Sam
replies.text: Then I can read it to Biscuit. He likes stories.

after.speaker: You
after.text: I promise. Every story, in order, and then home.

after.speaker: Sam
after.text: Okay. Pinky promise counts double. You're the best {big} ever.

again.speaker: Sam
again.text: Biscuit and me are gonna guard your room till you get back.

looks.name: Your tablet
looks.note: Three digital copies of Genesis 1:1, and all three say something different. One has a whole verse missing. Which one is true? Nobody can say anymore.

looks.name: Grandma's shelf
looks.note: Grandma's old bookshelf. It once held real paper books. Now it holds photos, and one empty spot she calls "saved for the Book."

looks.name: Pet Biscuit
looks.note: Biscuit thumps his tail. He doesn't know where you're going, but he's sure you'll come back.

nobody.speaker: You
nobody.text: My family is just inside, and I haven't said goodbye to anyone yet.

depart.speaker: Codex
depart.text: Time machine online. Destination: In the beginning. Genesis, chapter 1.

depart.speaker: You
depart.text: Satchel. Scroll. Everyone I love, right here in my heart. Here we go.
